findings.title: Backup code consumption is a read-modify-write race
findings.body: The backup code is validated and then invalidated via a separate `prisma.user.update` using the decrypted array read earlier. Two concurrent login attempts with the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either write lands, so a single backup code can be redeemed more than once (and the second write can also resurrect codes nulled by the first, since the whole array is re-serialized from stale data). Use an atomic conditional update or a transaction with row locking so each code can only be consumed once.

findings.title: Backup codes are overwritten on every setup call and can never be regenerated afterwards
findings.body: `/totp/setup` unconditionally regenerates and stores new `backupCodes`, and `/totp/disable` nulls them. There is no endpoint or UI to view or regenerate codes once 2FA is enabled. Consequently, if the user closes the "Backup Codes" dialog (e.g. via the dialog X / `onOpenChange`) without copying or downloading, the codes are permanently unrecoverable while 2FA stays enabled, leaving the user with no recovery path. A regenerate endpoint (or showing codes again from settings) is needed.

findings.title: backupCodes state typed as never[] and blob URL never revoked
findings.body: `useState([])` infers `never[]`, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and `backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)` only type-check because the response body is `any`; any future typing of the response will break. Additionally the object URL created with `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked when a new one is created — it is never revoked when the modal unmounts, leaking the blob (containing the plaintext backup codes) for the lifetime of the document.

findings.title: Download button is nested in an anchor inside a form without type="button"
findings.body: The download `Button` is rendered inside an `<a download>` which itself is inside the `<Form>` for `handleEnable`, and the button sets no `type` and no `preventDefault`. If the shared Button does not default to `type="button"`, clicking Download will also submit the enable form (re-running `handleEnable` with an empty totpCode) and may interrupt the download. Add `type="button"` explicitly, as done for the copy/close buttons via `preventDefault`.

findings.title: No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The new authentication path (backup code verification in `next-auth-options.ts` and in `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable`) including single-use invalidation is untested; the test only clicks the download/copy/close buttons on the setup screen (with TODOs for content). A regression that accepts an invalid code, fails to invalidate a used code, or breaks the backup-code login screen would not be caught.

findings.title: Component exported as `TwoFactor` in BackupCode.tsx
findings.body: The default export in `BackupCode.tsx` is named `TwoFactor` (copy-paste from the TOTP component). This misleads readers and shows up as `TwoFactor` in React DevTools/stack traces for two different components. Rename to `BackupCode`.
